tasks.title: log-inbound command with project_scope migration
tasks.goal: Record a relayed form or phone inquiry as an inbound_inquiry lead holding only the supplied fields (R-1, R-3 label storage).
tasks.plan:
1. Add cottonwood/migrations/003_inbound.sql: ALTER TABLE leads ADD COLUMN project_scope TEXT.
2. Add timeutil.parse_received(value): 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM' as America/Denver local (fold=0) or a UTC ISO string ending in Z/+00:00; returns stored UTC via to_utc_iso; ValueError otherwise.
3. Add cottonwood/inbound.py: Inquiry dataclass, validate() (at least one of name/email/phone; normalize_email/normalize_phone; budget as finite Decimal >= 0 stored as str), log_inquiry(conn, inquiry, duplicate_of=()) inserting organization (reuse by name_norm), contact, lead (type inbound_inquiry, stage candidate, value_basis buyer-stated when budget given) and one inquiry_logged activity with payload {channel, segment, is_test, duplicate_of} in one transaction.
4. Register log-inbound in cli.COMMANDS with --channel/--received/--segment required, optional --name --email --phone --company --location --scope --budget --test --actor --db; validation errors print 'error: <field>: ...' and exit 1.
5. Update the newest-version assertions (2 -> 3) in tests/test_migrate.py, tests/test_schema.py and tests/test_runbook_restore.py; add tests/test_inbound.py.
acceptance_criteria: After `cottonwood migrate` on a fresh file, PRAGMA user_version is 3 and PRAGMA table_info(leads) lists a nullable project_scope column (tests/test_inbound.py).

`cottonwood log-inbound --channel form --received "2026-11-16 09:30" --segment commercial --name "Pat Lee" --email Pat@Example.com` exits 0 and creates one leads row with type inbound_inquiry, stage candidate, channel form, segment commercial, received_at 2026-11-16T16:30:00Z, is_test 0 and NULL project_scope, value_amount, value_basis and property_location; its contact has name 'Pat Lee', email 'Pat@Example.com', email_norm 'pat@example.com' and NULL phone_e164.

With --phone "(801) 555-0134" --scope "lobby refresh" --budget 25000 --location "Murray, UT" --company "Acme Holdings" the lead stores project_scope 'lobby refresh', value_amount '25000', value_basis 'buyer-stated', property_location 'Murray, UT' and an organization named 'Acme Holdings'; the contact has phone_e164 '+18015550134'; a second inquiry with --company "ACME holdings" reuses the same organization id.

Each logged inquiry appends exactly one inquiry_logged activity for its lead whose JSON payload has channel, segment and is_test keys and does not contain the name, email, phone, scope or budget values.

--received 2026-11-16T16:30:00Z stores 2026-11-16T16:30:00Z; omitting --received, --channel or --segment, or passing a channel or segment outside the allowed values, exits non-zero and leaves leads empty.

An invalid email, an invalid phone, a budget of 'abc' or '-5', an unparseable --received, or no --name/--email/--phone each exit 1 with a stderr message naming the field, and leave leads, contacts, organizations and activities empty.
--test stores is_test 1 and the printed success message contains TEST; without --test the message does not contain TEST.
`uv run pytest`, `uv run ruff check .`, `uv run mypy .` and `uv run ruff format --check .` all pass.

tasks.title: Same-day duplicate check for log-inbound
tasks.goal: Warn on an inquiry matching an existing inquiry's normalized email or E.164 phone on the same America/Denver date, and save it only on explicit confirmation (R-2).
tasks.plan:
1. Add inbound.find_same_day_duplicates(conn, email_norm, phone_e164, received_at) -> list[int]: inbound_inquiry leads joined to contacts on (email_norm = ? OR phone_e164 = ?), filtered in Python to timeutil.local_date(received_at) equal to the new inquiry's local date, ordered by lead id.
2. In the log-inbound handler, after validation and before any write: on matches print 'warning: possible duplicate of lead(s) <ids> received <local date>' to stderr; if --confirm-duplicate, save with duplicate_of=ids; elif sys.stdin.isatty(), prompt 'Save anyway? [y/N] ' via input() and save only on y/yes (case-insensitive, trimmed); else print 'refused: duplicate not confirmed (use --confirm-duplicate)' and exit 1.
3. Add tests/test_inbound_duplicates.py covering email and phone matches, normalization, the cross-midnight local-date case, flag, prompt yes/no and non-TTY refusal.
acceptance_criteria: With an existing inbound inquiry for pat@example.com received 2026-11-16 09:30 local, logging another with --email 'PAT@example.com ' received 2026-11-16 15:00 local on non-interactive stdin prints a warning containing the existing lead id, exits 1 and adds no leads, contacts, organizations or activities rows.
A match on phone alone ('801.555.0134' vs an existing '(801) 555-0134', same local date) also warns and refuses without confirmation.
The same duplicate with --confirm-duplicate exits 0, creates the lead, and its inquiry_logged payload has duplicate_of equal to the list of matching lead ids.
With sys.stdin.isatty() true, answering 'y' or 'YES' to the prompt saves the inquiry (exit 0); answering 'n' or an empty line exits 1 and writes nothing.

An existing inquiry received 2026-11-16 23:30 local and a new one received 2026-11-17 00:30 local with the same email (same UTC date) produce no warning and save with exit 0; a non-matching email and phone on the same day also save with no warning.
`uv run pytest`, `uv run ruff check .`, `uv run mypy .` and `uv run ruff format --check .` all pass.

tasks.title: review command: inbound inquiries with tests labeled and excluded
tasks.goal: Print or write a Markdown review of inbound inquiries in which test inquiries are labeled TEST and excluded from counts (R-3, R-31 for review).
tasks.plan:
1. Add cottonwood/review.py: COUNTED_LEADS_FILTER = 'is_test = 0' (documented for report reuse); inbound_rows(conn) joining leads (type inbound_inquiry) to contacts and organizations, newest received_at first then id; inbound_counts(conn) -> totals by channel (form, phone) and segment (commercial, residential, unknown) over non-test rows plus the excluded test count; render_review(conn, generated_at) -> Markdown with '# Review', '## Inbound inquiries', the count line 'Inquiries: N (form a, phone b; commercial c, residential d, unknown e). Test inquiries excluded: M.' and a table with Lead, Received (display_local), Channel, Segment, Stage, Name, Email, Phone, Company, Location, Scope, Budget, Label; NULL prints as '—', '|' is escaped, Label is TEST for tests.
2. Register review in cli.COMMANDS with --out PATH and --db; --out creates parent folders, writes UTF-8, prints 'review written: <path>'; a missing database exits 1 with the error.
3. Add tests/test_review.py.
acceptance_criteria: `cottonwood review` on a database with logged inquiries prints Markdown containing '## Inbound inquiries' and one table row per inbound inquiry, newest received first, showing the lead id, received time as 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM -07:00' in America/Denver, channel, segment, stage and the supplied name, email and phone; empty fields print as '—'.
Rows for inquiries logged with --test contain the label TEST and rows for other inquiries do not.

With one test form inquiry, one test phone inquiry and one non-test form commercial inquiry, the count line reads 'Inquiries: 1 (form 1, phone 0; commercial 1, residential 0, unknown 0). Test inquiries excluded: 2.'; on an empty migrated database it reads 'Inquiries: 0 (form 0, phone 0; commercial 0, residential 0, unknown 0). Test inquiries excluded: 0.'

`cottonwood review --out out/review.md` run in a temporary folder creates the missing out folder, writes the same Markdown the command prints without --out, prints the path and exits 0; with a --db path that does not exist it exits 1 with an error message and writes no file.
A lead whose contact has deleted_at set and name, email and phone NULL is still listed, with '—' in those columns, and review exits 0.
`uv run pytest`, `uv run ruff check .`, `uv run mypy .` and `uv run ruff format --check .` all pass.
